species.name: Yellow perch
why: Water 35°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 6–32 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is mixed top to bottom, so fish can use many depths.

species.name: Northern pike
why: Water 35°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 2–18 ft deep, mostly on wind-blown banks.
The lake is mixed top to bottom, so fish can use many depths.
West wind at 21 mph pushes bait onto the east shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Walleye
why: Water 35°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 8–32 ft deep, mostly on wind-blown banks.
The lake is mixed top to bottom, so fish can use many depths.

Clear water: they bite best at dawn, dusk and on cloudy days.
